sentences.en: His deepest need was that people should like him.
sentences.zh: 他内心深处最渴望的，是赢得所有人的喜爱。

sentences.en: An admirable trait, that, in a spaniel or a whore.
sentences.zh: 对于一只长耳猎犬或是一个妓女来说，这倒是个令人赞赏的品质。

sentences.en: Not, I think, in a prime minister.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，作为首相就不行了。

sentences.en: And we've done him a favour too, if he did but know it.
sentences.zh: 我们也算是帮了他一把，如果他自己心知肚明的话。

sentences.en: He was in the trap and screaming from the moment he took office.
sentences.zh: 他从上台的那一刻起，就落入了陷阱并苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: We've simply put the poor bastard out of his agony.
sentences.zh: 我们不过是帮这个可怜的混蛋从痛苦中解脱出来罢了。

sentences.en: After life's fitful fever, he sleeps well.
sentences.zh: 经历了人生的狂热喧嚣之后，他终于安眠了。

sentences.en: So let's not involve ourselves in any squeamishness, all right?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们别在这里假惺惺的了，好吗？

sentences.en: Because this is just the start.
sentences.zh: 因为这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: That Dominic Sandbrook was Francis Urquhart, Chief Whip.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是多米尼克·桑德布鲁克饰演的首席党鞭弗朗西斯·厄克特。

sentences.en: That was chilling.
sentences.zh: 那段表演真让人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: That was absolutely chilling.
sentences.zh: 简直是不寒而栗。

sentences.en: As played by Ian Richardson in the BBC 1990 drama House of Cards, which was screened at exactly the moment that Mrs Thatcher was being defenestrated by the Tory party.
sentences.zh: 该角色由伊恩·理查森在英国广播公司1990年的电视剧《纸牌屋》中饰演，该剧播出的时间，恰好赶上撒切尔夫人被保守党赶下台的那一刻。

sentences.en: And the reason that I've used that as an introduction,
sentences.zh: 我之所以用这个来作为开场白，

sentences.en: and the reason that we're doing this special Rest is History episode, is because the Tory party is engaged, it seems, in another process of regicide.
sentences.zh: 以及我们之所以要做这期特别的《历史的休息》播客，是因为保守党似乎又在进行一场弑君般逼宫。

sentences.en: So we are recording this at quarter past nine on Monday the 6th of June.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是在6月6日星期一晚上九点一刻录制这期节目。

sentences.en: And 15 minutes ago, the results of a vote of confidence on the Prime Minister Boris Johnson were announced.
sentences.zh: 就在15分钟前，首相鲍里斯·约翰逊的信任投票结果公布了。

sentences.en: And he won it, but kind of not brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 他赢了，但赢得实在不算漂亮。

sentences.en: He won 2-1-1, 211 votes.
sentences.zh: 他赢了211票，211票赞成。

sentences.en: And 148 Tory MPs said they had no confidence in him.
sentences.zh: 但有148名保守党议员表示对他不信任。

sentences.en: So that's 41% of his parliamentary party said they didn't have confidence in him.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他所在党派中百分之四十一的议员表示对他不信任。

sentences.en: And for context, that's the worst performance, I think, by a Conservative leader in a confidence vote in my lifetime.
sentences.zh: 从背景来看，这在我有生之年里，保守党领袖在信任投票中表现最差的一次。

sentences.en: So it's worse, crucially, than Theresa May, his predecessor, in 2019, because she won 200 votes with 117 again.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，这比他的前任特雷莎·梅在2019年的表现还要糟糕，因为当时她获得了200票，而反对票是117票。

sentences.en: So the percentages were in her favour relative to Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 所以从百分比来看，特雷莎·梅的情况比鲍里斯·约翰逊要好。

sentences.en: So he is, you know, with four out of 10 Tory MPs lacking confidence in him, he is, shall we say, at the very least, grievously wounded.
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于十分之四的保守党议员对缺乏信任，他至少可以说，已经受了重伤。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, I have a metaphor here drawn from the world of natural history, which I know you're a big fan of.
sentences.zh: 好吧，多米尼克，我这里准备了一个自然界维度的隐喻，我知道你是这方面的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Big fan.
sentences.zh: 超级粉丝。

sentences.en: So Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizard, they have incredibly toxic teeth and breath and tongues.
sentences.zh: 科莫多巨蜥，也就是世界上最大的蜥蜴，它们的牙齿、口气和舌头都带有极强的毒性。

sentences.en: And all they have to do is give, you know, a passing mammal, a deer or whatever, a little nip, and all the bacteria get to work.
sentences.zh: 它们要做的，就是给路过的一只哺乳动物，比如鹿什么的，轻轻咬上一小口，然后那些细菌就开始发挥作用了。

sentences.en: And then the Komodo just kind of follows the deer.
sentences.zh: 接着，科莫多巨蜥就会一路尾随那头鹿。

sentences.en: The deer slowly gets more and more sick, and then it collapses, and then the Komodo dragon eats it.
sentences.zh: 这头鹿的病情会慢慢恶化，然后虚脱倒地，最后成为科莫多巨蜥的腹中餐。

sentences.en: So who's the Komodo dragon?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁是科莫多巨蜥呢？

sentences.en: Jeremy Hunt in this analogy.
sentences.zh: 在这个比喻里，杰瑞米·亨特就是。

sentences.en: I suppose the Tory party, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是保守党吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think this result does justify perhaps looking at the history of prime ministerial downfalls.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，这个结果确实有必要让我们回顾一下历史上那些首相的垮台。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: And you, I've been in the library all day looking at the murder of Caesars and things, but British prime minister as well.
sentences.zh: 而你呢，我一整天都在图书馆里研究刺杀凯撒之类的事情，当然也包括英国首相。

sentences.en: Very appropriate.
sentences.zh: 非常贴切。

sentences.en: Very appropriate.
sentences.zh: 非常贴切。

sentences.en: But you have been drawing up your list of the top 10 prime ministerial defenestrations.
sentences.zh: 不过你已经列出了一份关于首相下台的十大经典案例清单。

sentences.en: Because obviously, most prime ministers, by and large, resign because they've lost an election.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，大多数首相基本上都是因为输掉大选而辞职的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or they retire.
sentences.zh: 或者他们选择退休。

sentences.en: Or they retire.
sentences.zh: 或者退休。

sentences.en: Sort of Stanley Baldwin style.
sentences.zh: 有点像斯坦利·鲍德温那种风格。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你说的对。

sentences.en: So there are two ways that people normally go.
sentences.zh: 所以人们通常有两条退路。

sentences.en: Either they go like Stanley Baldwin, so they retire at a time of their own choosing.
sentences.zh: 要么像斯坦利·鲍德温那样，在自己选择的时机功成身退。

sentences.en: That's pretty rare.
sentences.zh: 这相当罕见。

sentences.en: They're Gladstone as well, I suppose you would say.
sentences.zh: 我想你也可以说还有格莱斯顿。

sentences.en: Or they are defeated.
sentences.zh: 或者他们被击败了。

sentences.en: They lose an election.
sentences.zh: 他们输掉了大选。

sentences.en: And then that's the end of their premierships.
sentences.zh: 然后他们的首相生涯就此结束。

sentences.en: That's what you might call the Jim Callaghan model.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的詹姆斯·卡拉汉模式。

sentences.en: Or the John Major.
sentences.zh: 或者约翰·梅杰模式。

sentences.en: Or Gordon Brown.
sentences.zh: 或者戈登·布朗模式。

sentences.en: Well, but obviously the most enjoyable ones, as your House of Cards analogy suggests, the most enjoyable ones are the regicides, the internal party coups.
sentences.zh: 不过，正如你的《纸牌屋》隐喻所暗示的那样，最精彩的当然是那些“弑君”事件，也就是党内政变。

sentences.en: And anybody who was alive in 1990 who remembers that amazing symbiosis, the Thatcher downfall on the news, and House of Cards playing at exactly that point.
sentences.zh: 任何经历过1990年的人都会记得那种奇妙的共振：新闻里正播报着撒切尔夫人的下台，而《纸牌屋》恰好在那个时刻播放。

sentences.en: I just watched the opening again.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚又看了一遍片头。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it opens with Frances Urquhart sitting in the Whip's office, looking at a picture of Mrs. Thatcher, and then kind of saying, all careers must end.
sentences.zh: 开场时，弗朗西斯·厄克特坐在党鞭办公室里，看着一张撒切尔夫人的照片，然后说了句“所有的政治生涯终有尽头”。

sentences.en: And laying it flat on the table.
sentences.zh: 并且把照片平放在桌子上。

sentences.en: And this went out at exactly the time she was resigned.
sentences.zh: 而这段剧集播出的时间，正好赶在她宣布辞职的时候。

sentences.en: It's extraordinary timing.
sentences.zh: 这时间简直绝了。

sentences.en: It's extraordinary serendipity.
sentences.zh: 这简直是不可思议的巧合。

sentences.en: Although it's not serendipity, though, that's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并不是真正的巧合，这才是最有趣的地方。

sentences.en: Because there was a sense at the end of the 1980s that Mrs. Thatcher's race was run.
sentences.zh: 因为在上世纪80年代末，人们就已经隐约感觉到撒切尔夫人的政治生命走到头了。

sentences.en: And I think there's that sense of gathering momentum.
sentences.zh: 我想那种大势所趋的氛围已经开始凝聚了。

sentences.en: There's that sense that in Westminster the tide has turned against you.
sentences.zh: 你会感觉到在威斯敏斯特，政治风向已经对你不利。

sentences.en: You see it reflected in the pages of the newspapers day after day.
sentences.zh: 你日复一日地从各大报纸的版面上看到这种反映。

sentences.en: And everybody knows.
sentences.zh: 每个人都心知肚明。

sentences.en: It's like the end of a season of Game of Thrones when everybody knows so-and-so's head is going to fall.
sentences.zh: 就像《权力的游戏》某一季接近尾声时，大家都知道某人的脑袋保不住了一样。

sentences.en: A quickening in the Praetorian.
sentences.zh: 禁卫军里开始出现骚动。

sentences.en: A camp.
sentences.zh: 阵营开始形成。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So that being so, you've drawn up your list, top 10.
sentences.zh: 既然如此，你已经列出了前十名的清单。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What is your first one?
sentences.zh: 你的第一位是谁？

sentences.en: So the first one is chronologically, right?
sentences.zh: 按时间顺序排的话，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, let's do it chronologically.
sentences.zh: 好，我们就按时间顺序来。

sentences.en: And the first one is the first one.
sentences.zh: 排在第一位的就是历史上的第一位。

sentences.en: So it's Sir Robert Walpole.
sentences.zh: 也就是罗伯特·沃波尔爵士。

sentences.en: So Robert Walpole, as most of our listeners will know, the first prime minister, he becomes prime minister in 1721.
sentences.zh: 正如我们大部分听众所知，罗伯特·沃波尔是英国第一任首相，他在1721年成为首相。

sentences.en: So he's been prime minister, by 1742, he's been prime minister, Tom, for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 所以到1742年的时候，汤姆，他当首相已经超过二十年了。

sentences.en: He's a great character.
sentences.zh: 他是个很有个性的人物。

sentences.en: He's quite Boris Johnsonian.
sentences.zh: 他有点像鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: So he's very earthy and he makes a virtue of his humanity.
sentences.zh: 他非常接地气，并且以自己的凡夫俗子为傲。

sentences.en: And he sort of says he's no, you know, he's no Puritan.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上说自己不是，你知道的，他可不是什么清教徒。

sentences.en: He's no, yeah, he's no reformer or all this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 他也不是，对，他不是什么改革派或者诸如此类的人。

sentences.en: He's incredibly corrupt.
sentences.zh: 他极其腐败。

sentences.en: He's basically, he has made Britain rich, but he's also kept Britain out of foreign wars, which has upset a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他让英国变得富裕，但也让英国置身于外国战争之外，这惹恼了很多人。

sentences.en: So the so-called Patriot wigs.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的“爱国辉格党人”。

sentences.en: And there's a definite sense, I think, by the beginning of the 1740s that, you know, he's old.
sentences.zh: 我想到了1740年代初，有一种非常明确的感觉，那就是他老了。

sentences.en: The momentum has moved, turned against him.
sentences.zh: 政治势头已经转变，开始对我不利。

sentences.en: He is forced slightly against his will to get Britain into war with Spain and the war of Jenkins's ear.
sentences.zh: 他有点违背意愿地把英国拖入了与西班牙的战争，也就是詹金斯耳战役。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which you may remember from our episode on weird wars.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得我们关于奇葩战争的那期节目。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Jenkins was a, he was a British merchant who had his ear chopped off.
sentences.zh: 所以詹金斯是一个英国商人，他的耳朵被割了下来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Supposedly by the Spanish years before, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 据说几年前被西班牙人割的，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely disgraceful Spanish behavior, which was obviously, obviously the pretext for this war, basically, because, you know, we wanted to be,
sentences.zh: 西班牙人的行为简直令人发指，这显然、显然成了这场战争的借口，基本上是因为我们想要，

sentences.en: to supplant Spain in the Caribbean and so on.
sentences.zh: 在加勒比海等地取代西班牙的地位。

sentences.en: But that doesn't go terribly well.
sentences.zh: 但这进展得并不太顺利。

sentences.en: So we'd lost the Battle of Cartagena in 1741.
sentences.zh: 我们在1741年的卡塔赫纳战役中失利了。

sentences.en: And here's the interesting thing that's, that's, that sets a bit of a sort of template.
sentences.zh: 有趣的地方就在这里，这奠定某种模式。

sentences.en: So in January 1742, there was a move in the, in Parliament to have a commission to investigate the handling of the war.
sentences.zh: 所以在1742年1月，议会中有人动议成立一个委员会来调查对这场战争的处理情况。

sentences.en: And that was basically seen, that's an attack, a full-scale attack on Walpole, because Walpole is, is administering the war.
sentences.zh: 这基本上被视为一次攻击，对沃波尔的全方位攻击，因为沃波尔正在管理这场战争。

sentences.en: And that was defeated by only three votes.
sentences.zh: 而这项动议仅仅以三票之差被否决了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So in a way, that's your, that's what, that's what so often happens in these stories.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，这就是，这就是在这些故事中经常发生的事情。

sentences.en: You get a Pyrrhic victory, and then just a little later, the final blow kind of falls.
sentences.zh: 你赢得了一场惨胜，然后没过多久，致命的一击就落了下来。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what happens.
sentences.zh: 事实也的确如此。

sentences.en: And the sort of Komodo dragon in this, the sort of final blow of the Komodo dragon in this case, is, it's very bizarre.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，所谓的“科莫多巨蜥”的致命一击，非常诡异。

sentences.en: It's an argument about a by-election in Chippenham.
sentences.zh: 那是一场关于奇彭纳姆补选的争论。

sentences.en: So that's one of the weird things about, about old, old political history is that often the sort of, the trigger is the most banal.
sentences.zh: 所以陈旧政治历史的怪异之处在于，导火索往往是最微不足道的。

sentences.en: But, but by-elections, I mean, you know, so hanging over Boris Johnson now are the results of the two by-elections coming up in the Red Wall.
sentences.zh: 但是，补选，我的意思是，你知道的，现在悬在鲍里斯·约翰逊头顶的，是“红墙”地区即将进行的两次补选结果。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: And in, in the Tory heartland.
sentences.zh: 还有保守党腹地的情况。

sentences.en: So actually by-elections are a kind of crucial markers of political health, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以实际上补选是衡量政治健康状况的关键指标，对吧？

sentences.en: So what had happened is that in 1741, there had been a general election, which has, as so often happened in those days, took about 18 months or something to be a general election.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的，在1741年举行了一次大选，和那个年代经常发生的情况一样，那次大选花了大约18个月左右的时间才完成。

sentences.en: And Chippenham had two seats, had two MPs.
sentences.zh: 奇彭纳姆有两个席位，有两名国会议员。

sentences.en: You know, obviously, Manchester or Birmingham have none, but Chippenham has two.
sentences.zh: 你看，很明显曼彻斯特或伯明翰一个都没有，但奇彭纳姆却有两个。

sentences.en: So Chippenham had two, and they'd both been won by the opposition, by sort of patriots or Tories.
sentences.zh: 所以奇彭纳姆有两个席位，并且都由反对派赢得，也就是所谓的爱国者或保守党人。

sentences.en: And, um, uh, the government, the, the, the government, two government candidates said they'd been very hard done by, and it had been rigged and all this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 然后，政府的两位候选人声称他们受到了极大的不公对待，选举被操纵了，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And, um, in the end of January, there was a vote in the House of Commons to sort of have, to, to throw out the Chippenham MPs and to have by-elections,
sentences.zh: 于是，在1月下旬，下议院进行了一次投票，试图罢免奇彭纳姆的议员并重新举行补选，

sentences.en: which the government hoped they would win.
sentences.zh: 政府希望他们能赢得补选。

sentences.en: And it became a confidence measure.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一场信任投票。

sentences.en: And, uh, Walpole lost it.
sentences.zh: 结果沃波尔输了。

sentences.en: Do you know how many, how many votes he, uh, he lost it by, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你知道他输了多少票吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: He lost it by one.
sentences.zh: 他以一票之差落败。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: By one vote.
sentences.zh: 就差一票。

sentences.en: Two, three, five, two, three, six.
That was the result.
sentences.zh: 这就是投票结果。

sentences.en: And if he'd won it, if he'd, if he'd won it by one, would he have staggered on?
sentences.zh: 如果他赢了，如果他以一票险胜，他还能勉强撑下去吗？

sentences.en: No, he didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他撑不下去了。

sentences.en: He was toast anyway, because that, that, that thing that happened, James Callaghan had a metaphor in 1979, very famously, just before he lost to Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 他无论如何都完蛋了，因为就像詹姆斯·卡拉汉在1979年即将输给撒切尔夫人前的一个非常著名的比喻所说的那样，

sentences.en: He said, there are times in politics when there's a sea change, no matter what you do, you know, as prime minister, the tide is against you.
sentences.zh: 他说，政治有时会出现巨变，无论你做什么，作为首相，大势已经背离了你。

sentences.en: And clearly for Walpole, um, the tide was against him.
sentences.zh: 显然对沃波尔来说，大势已去。

sentences.en: So he resigned, um, about, it's about 10 days later.

sentences.en: It was 218 votes and John Redwood, his challenger, won 89.
sentences.zh: 那是218票，而他的挑战者约翰·雷德伍德获得了89票。

sentences.en: So a pretty sizable margin.
sentences.zh: 所以优势相当明显。

sentences.en: Major's private target, Tom, was 215.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，梅杰的私人目标是215票。

sentences.en: So he only beat him by three.
sentences.zh: 所以他只比目标多赢了三票。

sentences.en: And he decided he would resign if he didn't get 215.
sentences.zh: 他曾决定如果拿不到215票就辞职。

sentences.en: But again, Major is, I think it's fair to say, a man with, I mean, not a perfect man, but a man with perhaps a little more integrity than Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，梅杰，我认为公平地说，是一个有——我的意思是，不是个完美的人，但可能比鲍里斯·约翰逊更有那么一点点正直的人。

sentences.en: And I say that as I'm not a sort of great Boris hater, but I think it would be very hard for anybody to claim that he was a man, a paragon of virtue.
sentences.zh: 我说这话并不是因为我是那种极度痛恨鲍里斯的人，但我认为很难有人声称他是一个道德上的完人。

sentences.en: Um, well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，是的。

sentences.en: And the, um, the, the, the Corleone comparison, um, he's, he's, he'd have to be dragged, dragged out in a coffin, basically.
sentences.zh: 还有，嗯，那个科里昂式的比较，嗯，他，他基本上得用棺材抬出去。

sentences.en: I mean, they've got two by-elections coming, uh, which I think they'll probably both, they'll lose both of them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们接下来有两场补选，嗯，我想他们大概会两场都输掉。

sentences.en: And they're important, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 而且这很重要，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they're, one's the Red Wall and one is kind of Tory heartlands.
sentences.zh: 因为它们是，一处是红墙选区，另一处有点像保守党的腹地。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, especially one of the things that did for Margaret Thatcher was the economy turning against her.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，特别是导致玛格丽特·撒切尔下台的原因之一是经济对她不利。

sentences.en: She lost control of inflation, interest rates went up, sort of Tory homeowners feeling the pinch with inflation going up and likely to go higher.
sentences.zh: 她失去了对通货膨胀的控制，利率上升，这让保守党的房主们随着通胀上升和可能进一步走高而感受到了压力。

sentences.en: But by the end of the year, it's very hard to see how things will get easier for Boris
sentences.zh: 但到今年年底，很难看出事情会怎么对鲍里斯·

sentences.en: Johnson.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊变得容易起来。

sentences.en: And, you know, he, he will make, if I wasn't, if I was a Tory party MP, I would think about it this way.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他，如果我不是，如果我是保守党议员，我会这样想。

sentences.en: Um, he's going to become a very convenient scapegoat a year from now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一年后他将成为一个非常方便的替罪羊。

sentences.en: You dump him, then you get a new leader and you go in saying, well, we've turned a page, you know, we've, we've learned the lessons, all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 你甩了他，然后换个新领袖上台说，好了，我们翻过了一页，你知道，我们吸取了教训，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So I think we could easily be here doing this, um, podcast again at 10, at half past 10.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我们很可能会在这里，嗯，在十点半再次做这个播客。

sentences.en: Um, well, we could put the same podcast with the same disagreements about Harold Wilson.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们可以把同一个播客拿出来，对哈罗德·威尔逊有同样的争论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: We just change it, tweak it a bit at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我们只需稍微改改，在开头微调一下。

sentences.en: That's a terrible insight into your, I hope the listeners aren't too shocked by that.
sentences.zh: 这是对你内心世界的一次可怕的剖析，我希望听众们不会对此感到太震惊。

sentences.en: But that's the kind of, um, beady eyed wheeler dealing that you stay ahead in politics, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这就是那种，嗯，精明的投机取巧，才能让你在政坛保持领先，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's what David Lord George would have done.
sentences.zh: 大卫·劳埃德·乔治就会这么做。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That's the David Lord George option.
sentences.zh: 这就是大卫·劳埃德·乔治的选择。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think we've done enough.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经说得够多了。

sentences.en: Um, and our poor producers have to go off and lick this into shape.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们的可怜制作人们得去把这期节目剪辑成形了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Tom, you know, we should probably, Tom's going to go catch up with Love Island.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你知道，我们大概应该，汤姆要去看《爱情岛》了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I am.
sentences.zh: 对，我要去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I think we should do the, uh, the Love Island episode, but we can discuss this.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该做，嗯，那一集《爱情岛》的节目，我们可以讨论这个。

sentences.en: We definitely should do it.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对应该做。

sentences.en: We're so going to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们一定要做。

sentences.en: And all the extra listeners we were attracted, um, because of our talk of, of, of the Earl of Wilmington, um, I think they'll stay for, for Love Island.
sentences.zh: 所有被我们吸引来的额外听众，嗯，因为我们谈论了威尔明顿伯爵，嗯，我想他们会留下来看《爱情岛》的。

sentences.en: So yeah, yes, we win.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们赢了。

sentences.en: Let's hope.
sentences.zh: 但愿如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 行吧。

sentences.en: Well, um, thank you for joining this all very spontaneous, all very exciting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢大家收听这期非常即兴、非常精彩的节目。

sentences.en: Um, I hope you've enjoyed it and, uh, we will be back on Thursday, won't we?
sentences.zh: 嗯，希望你们喜欢，而且，嗯，我们周四会回来，对吧？

sentences.en: With, uh, Denunzio, the first fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 带来，嗯，邓农齐奥，第一个法西斯主义者。

sentences.en: The first fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 第一个法西斯主义者。

sentences.zh: 到时见。

sentences.zh: 拜拜。
